close_reason: incorrect: SEC0 verified that nc_constrained_types should NOT include bits from excluded entries; mid-chain code confirms this; bug was fixed in PKIX-onc.20
description: nc_constrained_types is initialized by ORing bits from both the anchor's permitted_subtrees and excluded_subtrees entries, not left at 0. This is critically correct. If it started at 0, an anchor constraining DNS via permittedSubtrees could have its permitted set emptied by a conflicting intermediate CA; check_name_constraints would then consult nc_constrained_types, find DNS bit unset, and silently accept all DNS names — the opposite of the intended behavior. The excluded case also requires seeding: a name type appearing only in anchor excludedSubtrees (no permitted entry) still needs its bit set so the excluded check fires correctly. A future contributor might suggest starting at 0 and only setting bits during chain-walk NC updates, reasoning that 'anchor NC is not a CA cert.' That is wrong: RFC 5280 §6.1.2(e)/(f) explicitly seeds the initial permitted and excluded state from the trust anchor.
title: nc_constrained_types seeded from anchor NC collections, not initialized to 0
